answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with concurrent stake lockup: each identity must keep its own deposit locked for the whole epoch, and the same deposit cannot back two identities at once. Think of a terrace where every plot needs its own quartz foundation stone, not one stone moved between plots: the kernel of the rule is non-reusability. A single honest agent locks one stake; an attacker wanting a thousand fake votes must lock a thousand stakes simultaneously, tying up capital that cannot be spent elsewhere, so fake influence scales only with real money at risk, not with cheap copies.
